5. UNAVOIDABLE ADVERSE ENVIRONMENTAL EFFECTS
5.1 HUMAN RESOURCES IMPACTED
The Bad Creek Project would not cause removal of any residences or businesses, since the project area is rather remote and uninhabited.
Construction of the project would have a short-term adverse effect on local transportation in two ways. The planned relocation of 0.4 mile of Route 171 would disrupt traffic for the period of its relocation. In addition, movement of heavy equipment and large numbers of construction workers could cause some traffic congestion and safety problems. Upon completion of the project, however, traffic would return to approximately the previous levels.
5.1.1 Scenic and Esthetic Resources
A natural resource that the proposed project site now offers is its visually pleasing, rugged, and wilderness-type landscape character. Inundation would drastically change portions of Bad and West Bad Creeks and the landscape character of the area. This impact is embodied in change, but how it affects individuals is difficult to determine, since a quantitative or qualitative evaluation of the change now would be subjective; only the test-of-time could yield a true evaluation.
5.2 USES PREEMPTED AND UNAVOIDABLE CHANGES
5.2.1 Flora
Regardless of the mitigative measures discussed in Section 4, about 505 acres of vegetation would be permanently lost due to clearing and inundation required for project construction, operation, and maintenance. Wildlife habitat, timber, agricultural (small amount of pasture land), and esthetic values associated with this vegetation would also be lost.
Although the Applicant proposes to transplant some species of rare plant species that would be adversely affected by the proposed action, many others would be lost. This would deplete an already limited population and eliminate the habitat supporting these rare forms.
